candidates.first_failed_contract: The trusted relationship view obtains the participant's personal observer minute and applies created/resolved timestamps to the wedding commitment, but first finds it only through the current exclusive_commitment_participant uniqueness row. A terminal commitment transition deletes that row and then keeps the effective-dated commitment history. After canonical wedding settlement at a later minute, a lagging participant whose personal minute falls between commitment creation and settlement cannot reach the still-historically-valid commitment through this view; the subsequent date filter cannot restore it.
candidates.conditional_example: Assume a commitment was created at minute 10 and a successful canonical wedding settlement at minute 100 removed its participant index, while one existing participant's personal observer minute remains 50. The view already has that character in its candidate population via the preserved courtship and returns a relationship summary, but its wedding fields are absent even though 10 <= 50 < 100. Spouse history separately remains after minute 100, and the courtship history is filtered to the observer minute. A participant lifecycle write can settle a due wedding at official time independent of the other participant's clock; other paths and supported circumstances still require audit. This is source chronology reasoning, not an executed state.
candidates.actual_consumers: The selected web residence source maps wedding_effective_minute into an optional countdown. The NPC dialogue helper selects a commitment only when the projected id and target partner exist, then uses it for countdown and action presentation. The party social answer also branches on the projected wedding field. These are source paths only; individual page access, actual gateway state, UI rendering and a player impact have not been observed. Mutation authority and whether cancellation at the official current time is allowed remain separate.
candidates.policy_qualification: The surrounding view uses observer-minute filters for marriage, courtship, pregnancy and the wedding row, supporting a historical-visibility interpretation. Whether every wedding field is intended to be historical or canonically current remains a policy question; choose and document it rather than infer an unqualified behavior guarantee.
candidates.connected_repair: After completing the audit, resolve historical versus canonical-current presentation policy for these fields. If historical visibility is required, select from authoritative effective-dated commitment history at the observer frontier rather than solely the current uniqueness marker; preserve unique active admission, privacy, valid terminal/cancellation states and actual current-time mutation rules. If current-only is intended, make the projection and consumers explicitly consistent. Reconcile the separate global wedding frontier and post-write error findings without collapsing their distinct first failures.
